## India: DPDPA Implementation & Compliance

MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed that there will be no extensions for compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), 2023, urging startups and other entities to prepare for the upcoming deadlines. This firm stance underscores the government's commitment to timely implementation, despite concerns about readiness across various sectors. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

Government ministries and state bodies are actively assessing their readiness for the DPDPA, facing a significant compliance test to align their data processing activities with the new legal framework. This internal review highlights the extensive operational changes required across public sector entities. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

The DPDPA introduces the concept of Consent Managers, which will significantly impact Global Capability Centres (GCCs) operating in India by streamlining consent management processes. These entities will need to integrate new technical and operational frameworks to leverage these mechanisms effectively. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

## India: DPDPA Legal Challenges & Interpretation

The Supreme Court of India has sought a response from the Centre regarding Public Interest Litigations (PILs) challenging the constitutionality of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. These petitions raise fundamental questions about the Act's compliance with constitutional rights and principles. ## India: Sectoral & Emerging Tech Focus

WhatsApp is proactively testing a date-of-birth feature in India, anticipating the age-verification rules mandated by the DPDPA. This move demonstrates how major tech platforms are adapting their services to comply with India's new data protection regime, particularly concerning the processing of children's data.
